newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel demands extradition of PLO top cop.
newsitem.headline: Israel demands extradition of PLO top cop.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Friday Israel had evidence Palestinian police chief Ghazi Jabali had ordered attacks on Jews in the West Bank and demanded his extradition from PLO-ruled territory.
"We have no doubt that Ghazi Jabali was involved directly in directing Palestinian police cells to carry out attacks," Mordechai told Israel's Channel One television.

"We ordered that Ghazi Jabali will be arrested if he enters territory under our control. We have enough evidence to put him on trial. We demand the Palestinian Authority act to extradite him," Mordechai said.
Mordechai stopped short of saying Israel would enter Palestinian-ruled territories to seize Jabali.

Israel had called for Jabali's arrest as part of a package of demands on the Palestinian Authority in the aftermath of a double suicide bombing in a Jerusalem market on Wednesday that killed 15, including the bombers.
Mordechai said Israel had not yet determined the identity of the bombers but said the Islamic militant group Hamas was behind the attack.
A leaflet issued in the name of Hamas's military wing claimed responsibilty for the blasts but Israeli officials questioned its authenticity.
In Gaza on Thursday, Jabali scoffed at Israel's demand.
"Israel can't arrest me. If they come to Gaza or any place else I am, they will not return," he told a news conference. "Do they think that Palestinian people are puppets?"

Israel suspended dialogue with the Palestinians, clamped a closure on the West Bank and Gaza, rounded up suspected Islamic militants and demanded Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat arrest militants in areas under his authority.

Asked whether Jabali's arrest was a condition to restore dialogue, Mordechai said: "We will view Palestinian behavior as events continue within the overall picture of our demands...we will decide what steps to take at each stage."
Palestinian forces also arrested suspected militants after Wednesday's attack. Mordechai said PLO forces had begun to act to a certain extent but not with "full intensity".

Aides to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu threatened Israeli troops could re-enter Palestinian areas to seize militants if Arafat failed to do the job. Palestinians warned such action would cross a "red line".
Mordechai said Israel wanted to press ahead with peace talks but said dialogue would only proceed "in parallel with the pace in which the Palestinian Authority does what is demanded of it."
